label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
**4 stars — Kept my trading setup up during a storm, but the fan and beeping are annoying**

I bought the Kestrel Bastion 1500 on Voltwise for $229 in August 2026. It’s rated at 1500VA / 1000W with pure sine wave output. I got it mainly because I day-trade crypto from home in Miami, and losing power in the middle of a trade is not something I wanted to find out about the hard way.

On October 14, a storm knocked out my power at around 2:20 p.m. I was 10x long on a SOL perp at the time, so yeah, pretty bad timing. My PC, monitors, modem, and router all stayed up, and I was able to close the position cleanly in about four minutes. That alone made me glad I had it.

For anyone trying to figure out if it’ll handle their setup, mine is a PC, three monitors, a modem, and a router. The Bastion’s display shows around **410W while I’m trading**. I also did a deliberate runtime test: I got **11 minutes and 40 seconds** at that load before I shut everything down. That’s how long I ran it, not necessarily the absolute maximum runtime.

The box says approximately 14 minutes at 500W, so my result wasn’t quite what I expected given my lower displayed load. Still, I’d rather plan around the time I actually saw than assume I’ll get the box number. For me, 11-plus minutes is enough time to manage a position and shut down, but I wouldn’t treat it like a way to keep trading through a long outage.

It has 10 outlets: five are battery-backed and five are surge-only. **Make sure your modem and router are plugged into the battery-backed side.** Keeping your PC and monitors on doesn’t help much if your internet goes down with the power. There’s also a 60W USB-C port.

The stuff that bugs me is mostly the noise. During the first week, the fan randomly kicked on at 3 a.m. and woke me up. It’s loud, kind of like a hair dryer on low. The outage beeping is loud as hell too. You can mute it in the app, but that setting resets after a firmware update, so check it again if you update.

The desktop app looks like something from Windows XP. I don’t really care how pretty it is, though, and the automatic shutdown works, which is the important part. The unit is also heavy at around 30 pounds. The battery is swappable, which is nice, but a replacement pack costs $95, so that’s worth factoring in.

Overall, I’m giving it four stars. It did exactly what I needed when the power went out, and the runtime was enough to get me out of a leveraged trade without panicking. I’m taking a star off for the fan, the obnoxious beeping, and that mute setting resetting after a firmware update.
